title: MultiModal-RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Imaging with Vision-Language Models
abstract: We present MultiModal-RAG, a framework for retrieval-augmented generation applied to medical imaging tasks. Our approach combines CLIP-based visual encoders with large language models to provide grounded, evidence-based responses to clinical queries. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with reduced hallucination rates.

summary.summary_100_words: MultiModal-RAG introduces a novel retrieval-augmented generation framework for medical imaging. The system combines CLIP encoders for visual feature extraction with large language models for generating grounded clinical responses. A cross-modal retrieval mechanism ensures that generated answers are grounded in retrieved visual and textual evidence, minimizing hallucinations. The framework is evaluated on MIMIC-CXR, VQA-RAD, and PathVQA, achieving state-of-the-art performance across all benchmarks.
summary.methodology: Cross-modal retrieval using CLIP visual embeddings and FAISS index, followed by LLM generation conditioned on top-K retrieved evidence.
summary.architecture: CLIP visual encoder → FAISS retrieval → LLM (GPT-4V) → grounded answer generation
summary.experiments: Compared against UniVLP, MedPaLM-2, and GPT-4V baselines on VQA accuracy and factuality metrics.
summary.results: 94.3% VQA accuracy on VQA-RAD, 17% reduction in hallucination rate vs GPT-4V baseline.
limitations: Only validated on English-language clinical notes
key_contributions: First RAG framework for medical VQA
